item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-40fa3c58a9bf16f9","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The U.S. Trade Representative reported that Mexico’s energy policies prioritized CFE- and PEMEX-linked state interests over private competitors, including cleaner wind and solar suppliers; cited measures included the 2021 electricity-law amendment, delays or revocations of private permits, preferential sulfur-standard treatment for PEMEX, and a gas-network policy favoring PEMEX or CFE. The United States considered these measures inconsistent with USMCA market-access, investment, and state-owned-enterprise obligations and initiated consultations.","question_ids":["2B.5","2B.7","2B.8","4B.2","5B.4","5B.5","5B.7","5B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source describes policies adopted or pursued before and during 2022, relevant as inherited context for López Obrador’s 2023 period; it does not establish later 2023 resolution.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the policy direction to Mexico since December 2018 and identifies López Obrador’s government as responsible for the measures.","limitations":["This is a U.S. government account of a trade dispute and presents the U.S. position; it does not provide Mexico’s response or a final adjudication.","The source does not establish the 2023 outcome of the consultations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fca7e9cfaf79ddc3","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The U.S. Trade Representative reported that Mexico’s energy policies prioritized CFE- and PEMEX-linked state interests over private competitors, including cleaner wind and solar suppliers; cited measures included the 2021 electricity-law amendment, delays or revocations of private permits, preferential sulfur-standard treatment for PEMEX, and a gas-network policy favoring PEMEX or CFE. The United States considered these measures inconsistent with USMCA market-access, investment, and state-owned-enterprise obligations and initiated consultations.","question_ids":["2B.5","2B.7","2B.8","4B.2","5B.4","5B.5","5B.7","5B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source describes policies adopted or pursued before and during 2022, relevant as inherited context for López Obrador’s 2023 period; it does not establish later 2023 resolution.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the policy direction to Mexico since December 2018 and identifies López Obrador’s government as responsible for the measures.","limitations":["This is a U.S. government account of a trade dispute and presents the U.S. position; it does not provide Mexico’s response or a final adjudication.","The source does not establish the 2023 outcome of the consultations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55613d962f1c62ce","start_unit":11,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"Reporters Without Borders stated that Mexico recorded 14 journalist killings in the first eight months of 2022, at least 10 directly related to journalism, with eight victims previously threatened; since López Obrador took office in December 2018, it counted at least 36 journalist killings and two disappearances, with near-total impunity in most cases. RSF said López Obrador had publicly condemned only five of the 14 killings and called for urgent reform of prevention, protection, and justice mechanisms.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.3","3B.4","3B.6","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6","4B.10","7B.2","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The evidence concerns 2018-2022 and supplies pre-2023 conditions relevant to the 2023 ruler-period; it does not report 2023 developments.","ruler_attribution":"RSF directly calls on López Obrador and his security cabinet to act and attributes federal inaction partly to his government, while also urging state governors to improve protection and investigations.","limitations":["The source does not establish the perpetrators’ identities or prove that every killing was caused by official policy.","It provides advocacy and monitoring claims, not a complete governmental investigation record."]},{"source_id":"SRC-151097b95aedb9e6","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"In his fourth government report, López Obrador emphasized distributional and qualitative outcomes over headline growth, claiming that labor income, social-program income for older people, and Indigenous income had improved. The same account reported that GDP remained 2.5% below its pre-pandemic level, though quarterly growth was positive and the IMF expected 2.4% growth for 2022.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.7","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.10","7B.1","7B.8","8B.1","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report was published in 2022 and describes conditions and claims entering the 2023 period; it does not measure full-year 2023 outcomes.","ruler_attribution":"The claims and policy framing are explicitly attributed to López Obrador’s fourth government report.","limitations":["Several favorable figures are reported as presidential claims; the article also provides countervailing macroeconomic context but does not independently verify every program figure.","The source does not establish causality between the programs and reported income changes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f18d7011abfc3e01","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"OECD data show Mexico’s tax-to-GDP ratio increased from 16.8% in 2022 to 17.7% in 2023, the highest recorded in the supplied series, but Mexico ranked 38th of 38 OECD countries in 2023. Mexico’s tax structure relied relatively more on corporate income, payroll, and VAT revenues and substantially less on social-security contributions than the OECD average.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.8","5B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023 and is suitable for the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The data describe Mexico during López Obrador’s administration but do not attribute the tax outcomes solely to him.","limitations":["The source is descriptive and does not identify the responsible policies, distributional incidence, or causal contribution of the president.","The tax-structure comparison uses 2022 structure data within the 2024 publication."]},{"source_id":"SRC-303fb885c5470f07","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"López Obrador backed Raquel Buenrostro’s replacement of Economy Ministry trade officials, including the removal of Deputy Trade Secretary Luz María de la Mora and lawyers handling foreign litigation, during active USMCA disputes over energy and automotive rules. The article reported that the constitutional electricity reform had failed for lack of support, statutory changes were blocked in court, and the energy regulator nevertheless continued creating obstacles for private plants; López Obrador defended the policy and denied any treaty violation.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.5","5B.2","5B.4","5B.7","7B.5","7B.8","8B.4","8B.5","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The source describes institutional and policy conditions in late 2022, relevant to the 2023 period but not a complete 2023 assessment.","ruler_attribution":"The article explicitly reports López Obrador’s confirmation and defense of the personnel changes and energy position.","limitations":["The article does not establish whether the replacements improved or harmed the eventual negotiations.","The report contains competing legal positions and does not provide a final judicial or treaty ruling."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d2870595f63b9905","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"UNICEF reported persistent Mexican education gaps: only 56 of 100 children entering primary school completed upper-secondary education without repeating or dropping out; PISA 2022 found 47% below minimum reading proficiency and 66% below minimum mathematics proficiency. Disparities were greater for Indigenous, rural, migrant, poor, and disabled children. UNICEF stated that the State is the principal guarantor and requires greater public investment, robust monitoring, and policies reaching excluded groups.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.6","6B.8","6B.9","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The page includes 2022-2025 indicators and current program context; it is relevant to assessing education conditions entering and during 2023, but does not isolate López Obrador-era changes.","ruler_attribution":"UNICEF assigns primary responsibility for fulfilling the education right to the Mexican State, not specifically to López Obrador.","limitations":["The source does not quantify federal spending or identify which administration caused the reported gaps.","Some cited indicators are dated 2023 or 2025 and therefore extend beyond the target year."]},{"source_id":"SRC-5cd18cba57aba177","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Segalmex, created by López Obrador’s government to pursue food self-sufficiency, faced investigations into alleged diversion of public funds. The article reported 22 complaints, 15 investigations, an audit finding that the agency could not account for more than 10 billion pesos, alleged direct awards of 797 million pesos to six companies linked to shell-company networks, and an investigation into an unauthorized 100-million-peso securities purchase. López Obrador acknowledged the investigation and removed director Ignacio Ovalle, but appointed him to another government post.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","6B.2","6B.4","6B.5","6B.7","7B.3","7B.4","7B.5","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10","8B.2","8B.4","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evidence concerns 2019-2022 and is relevant as a governance and implementation condition entering 2023; it does not establish final 2023 accountability outcomes.","ruler_attribution":"The agency’s creation and Ovalle’s appointment and reassignment are attributed to López Obrador’s government; the alleged misconduct is attributed to agency officials and investigated by Mexican authorities.","limitations":["The reported fraud and diversion were allegations or investigations at the article’s publication date, not final convictions.","The source does not establish López Obrador’s personal enrichment or direct knowledge of the alleged misconduct.","The article does not report the eventual recovery of funds or final legal outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-978871c313a38254","start_unit":4,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The World Bank described Mexico as having strong macroeconomic institutions, open trade, and diversified manufacturing, while reporting weak long-run growth and inclusion relative to peers. It stated that multidimensional poverty fell from 43.2% in 2016 to 36.3% in 2022, lifting 5.4 million people, driven mainly by labor-market outcomes including minimum-wage increases. The Bank identified needed improvements in infrastructure investment, private-capital mobilization, business conditions, security, regulatory certainty, public services, competition, and revenue mobilization.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.6","5B.8","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The poverty figures cover through 2022 and the institutional assessment is relevant to 2023; the page was updated later and includes forecasts beyond the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The World Bank describes national conditions and policy needs but does not attribute the outcomes exclusively to López Obrador.","limitations":["The page does not isolate federal versus subnational or external contributions.","Some text and forecasts postdate 2023 and should not be treated as contemporaneous evidence of the target year.","The poverty reduction statistic does not establish that López Obrador’s policies alone caused the change."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b14eb4f40dae3095","start_unit":20,"end_unit":23,"fact_summary":"The Committee to Protect Journalists’ 2023 Mexico archive recorded killings of journalists Luis Martín Sánchez Iñíguez and Nelson Matus Peña, the shooting death of Jesús Gutiérrez Vergara, attacks or abductions involving multiple journalists, and a 27.5-year sentence for the murder of Israel Vázquez. CPJ also reported that López Obrador repeatedly criticized Article 19 and news outlets, and reported allegations that Mexican authorities surveilled activist Raymundo Ramos’s communications with journalists.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.3","3B.4","3B.8","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","4B.10","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers events and official conduct in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"CPJ directly attributes the criticism of media and Article 19 to López Obrador; killings, investigations, sentencing, and surveillance allegations concern Mexican authorities or other actors.","limitations":["The archive summaries do not provide complete case files or final findings for each killing or surveillance allegation.","CPJ’s calls for investigation indicate unresolved attribution in several cases.","The sentence for Israel Vázquez demonstrates one accountability outcome but does not establish broader effectiveness."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-0e0deed4e78bdc09","SRC-4bad3713d28d861c"],"batch_limitations":["Most supplied documents concern 2022 or earlier and therefore provide context entering 2023 rather than direct full-year 2023 evidence.","The supplied AIFA document returned a 404 page and mostly contained current website terms and privacy material, with no material 2023 ruler-quality fact.","The supplied investment-and-inflation document was treated as having no material fact because its content was a near-duplicate contextual economic report already represented by the supplied USTR, OECD, World Bank, and EL PAÍS economic sources."]}
